_meta.note: Named points on bones. Positions are in each mesh's local space (p) with a surface normal (n). Points on a left bone are mirrored to the right bone automatically. Definitions are keyed by bone key and lower-case landmark name.
_meta.editor: Open the site with ?edit at the end of the address to place points, then use Export JSON and replace this file.
_meta.scans: Numbered points on Sketchfab scans, keyed by model uid: name, scene position (p), and the camera eye/target used when the point is selected.

head.description: Rounded articular surface at the caudal part of the proximal end. It articulates with the glenoid cavity of the scapula to form the shoulder joint.

greater tubercle.description: Large eminence on the lateral side of the proximal end. Insertion of the supraspinatus and infraspinatus.

lesser tubercle.description: Eminence on the medial side of the proximal end. Insertion of the subscapularis.

intermediate tubercle.description: Ridge in the horse that divides the intertubercular groove into two channels for the biceps tendon.

intertubercular groove.description: Groove between the tubercles that carries the tendon of origin of the biceps brachii.

deltoid tuberosity.description: Roughened prominence on the lateral surface of the shaft. Insertion of the deltoideus.

condyle.description: Distal articular surface that articulates with the radius and ulna at the elbow joint.

olecranon fossa.description: Deep caudal depression above the condyle that receives the anconeal process of the ulna when the elbow is extended.

lateral epicondyle.description: Lateral prominence of the distal end. Origin of the extensor muscles of the carpus and digits.

medial epicondyle.description: Medial prominence of the distal end. Origin of the flexor muscles of the carpus and digits.

head.description: Hemispherical proximal articular surface that fits into the acetabulum to form the hip joint.

fovea capitis.description: Pit or notch on the head for the ligament of the head of the femur; in the horse it also receives the accessory ligament.

neck.description: Constriction that joins the head to the shaft.

greater trochanter.description: Large lateral process at the proximal end. Insertion of the middle and deep gluteal muscles.

lesser trochanter.description: Medial process near the proximal end. Insertion of the iliopsoas.

third trochanter.description: Lateral prominence on the shaft, present in the horse. Insertion of the superficial gluteal muscle.

trochlea.description: Grooved cranial surface of the distal end on which the patella glides.

medial and lateral condyles.description: Caudal articular surfaces of the distal end that articulate with the tibia through the menisci.

supracondylar fossa.description: Depression above the lateral condyle, deep in the horse. Origin of the superficial digital flexor.

spine of scapula.description: Ridge that divides the lateral surface into the supraspinous and infraspinous fossae.

tuber of the spine.description: Thickening at the middle of the spine in the horse. Attachment of the trapezius.

supraspinous fossa.description: Area cranial to the spine. Origin of the supraspinatus.

infraspinous fossa.description: Area caudal to the spine. Origin of the infraspinatus.

glenoid cavity.description: Shallow distal socket that articulates with the head of the humerus.

supraglenoid tubercle.description: Prominence above the glenoid cavity. Origin of the biceps brachii.

scapular cartilage.description: Cartilage extending the dorsal border, large in the horse and ox.

nuchal crest.description: Transverse ridge at the caudodorsal border of the skull. Attachment of the nuchal ligament and neck muscles.

external sagittal crest.description: Median ridge on the parietal bones. The temporal muscle arises on either side of it.

temporal fossa.description: Depression on the side of the cranium, bounded by the temporal crest and the zygomatic arch. Filled by the temporal muscle.

temporal crest.description: Ridge that bounds the temporal fossa dorsally.

zygomatic arch.description: Bony bridge formed by the zygomatic process of the temporal bone and the temporal process of the zygomatic bone. The masseter arises from it.

zygomatic process of the frontal bone.description: Process that joins the zygomatic arch and closes the orbit caudally in the horse and ruminants.

supraorbital foramen.description: Opening in the zygomatic process of the frontal bone for the supraorbital nerve and vessels; a site for nerve blocks in the horse.

orbit.description: Bony cavity that holds the eyeball. In the horse it is a complete bony ring.

facial crest.description: Prominent ridge on the maxilla and zygomatic bone. Origin of the masseter and a landmark for the maxillary sinus.

infraorbital foramen.description: Rostral opening of the infraorbital canal on the maxilla, where the infraorbital nerve emerges; a site for nerve blocks.

nasoincisive notch.description: Notch between the nasal bone and the nasal process of the incisive bone, forming the margin of the bony nostril.

nasal process of the incisive bone.description: Slender process of the incisive bone that runs caudodorsally towards the nasal bone.

body of the incisive bone.description: Rostral part of the incisive bone that carries the alveoli of the upper incisors.

interincisive canal.description: Median canal between the bodies of the two incisive bones.

occipital condyles.description: Paired articular surfaces beside the foramen magnum that articulate with the atlas.

foramen magnum.description: Large opening in the occipital bone through which the brain continues as the spinal cord.

hypoglossal canal.description: Canal in the occipital bone for the hypoglossal nerve (cranial nerve XII).

jugular foramen.description: Opening for the glossopharyngeal, vagus and accessory nerves (cranial nerves IX, X and XI).

basilar part of the occipital bone.description: Part of the occipital bone that forms the floor of the caudal cranial cavity.

tympanic bulla.description: Rounded part of the temporal bone that encloses the middle ear cavity.

muscular tubercle.description: Tubercle on the base of the skull for the attachment of the ventral neck muscles.

foramen lacerum.description: Large irregular opening in the base of the horse skull between the occipital, sphenoid and temporal bones, for vessels and nerves.

retroarticular process.description: Process behind the mandibular fossa that limits caudal movement of the mandible.

mandibular fossa.description: Articular surface of the temporal bone for the condylar process of the mandible (temporomandibular joint).

articular tubercle.description: Rounded articular eminence rostral to the mandibular fossa.

pterygoid process.description: Process of the sphenoid bone that, with the palatine and pterygoid bones, bounds the choanae.

alar canal.description: Canal at the base of the pterygoid process of the sphenoid bone in the horse, for the maxillary artery.

choanae.description: Caudal openings of the nasal cavity into the nasopharynx.

maxillary tuber.description: Caudal end of the maxilla behind the last upper cheek tooth.

palatine fissure.description: Opening in the rostral part of the hard palate, between the incisive bone and the maxilla.

palatine process of the maxilla.description: Horizontal plate of the maxilla that forms most of the hard palate.

incisive part.description: Rostral part of the body of the mandible that carries the lower incisors and canines.

molar part.description: Caudal part of the body of the mandible that carries the lower cheek teeth.

ramus.description: Vertical part of the mandible that rises to the coronoid and condylar processes.

coronoid process.description: Rostral process of the ramus, projecting into the temporal fossa. Insertion of the temporal muscle.

condylar process.description: Caudal process of the ramus that articulates with the temporal bone at the temporomandibular joint.

mandibular notch.description: Notch between the coronoid and condylar processes.

masseteric fossa.description: Depression on the lateral surface of the ramus. Insertion of the masseter.

pterygoid fossa.description: Depression on the medial surface of the ramus. Insertion of the medial pterygoid muscle.

mandibular foramen.description: Opening on the medial surface of the ramus where the inferior alveolar nerve and vessels enter the mandibular canal.

mental foramen.description: Opening on the lateral surface of the incisive part where the mental nerve emerges; a site for nerve blocks.

interalveolar border.description: Toothless gap between the incisors or canine and the cheek teeth (the 'bars'), where the bit rests in the horse.

mandibular angle.description: Rounded caudoventral corner where the body meets the ramus.

vascular groove.description: Notch on the ventral border where the facial artery, facial vein and parotid duct cross onto the face; the facial pulse is taken here.

skull.description: The bones of the head. They are divided into cranial bones, which enclose the brain, meninges and ear, and facial bones, which form the skeleton of the oral and nasal cavities. Most are joined by immovable sutures. In the dog: Shape varies with breed: dolichocephalic, mesaticephalic or brachycephalic. The orbit is incomplete and closed laterally by the orbital ligament. The sagittal crest is often prominent.

mandible.description: The only movable bone of the skull; it carries the lower teeth. Each half has a horizontal body and a vertical ramus. In the dog: Fibrous symphysis. Large coronoid process and deep masseteric fossa.

cervical vertebrae.description: Seven cervical vertebrae in all domestic mammals. The first (atlas) and second (axis) are specialised for movements of the head. In the dog: 7. The axis has a long, blade-like spinous process.

thoracic vertebrae.description: They articulate with the ribs. In large animals their tall cranial spinous processes form the withers. In the dog: 13. The anticlinal vertebra is usually T11.

lumbar vertebrae.description: Vertebrae of the loin, with long, flat transverse processes. In the dog: 7.

sacrum.description: Fused sacral vertebrae. It articulates with the ilium at the sacroiliac joint and transmits the hindlimb's thrust to the spine. In the dog: 3 fused vertebrae.

caudal vertebrae.description: Tail vertebrae. Distally they become simple rods as the processes disappear. In the dog: About 20–23.

ribs.description: Paired bones forming the lateral walls of the thorax. Sternal ribs reach the sternum directly; asternal ribs join the costal arch. In the dog: 13 pairs: 9 sternal, 4 asternal. The last pair is usually floating.

scapula.description: Flat bone of the shoulder. It is attached to the trunk by muscles only (synsarcosis); the clavicle is absent or vestigial in domestic mammals. In the dog: Acromion present. The spine divides the bone into two nearly equal fossae.

humerus.description: Long bone of the arm, between the shoulder and the elbow. In the dog: A supratrochlear foramen above the trochlea connects the olecranon and radial fossae.

radius and ulna.description: The main weight-bearing bone of the forearm. Provides the olecranon (point of the elbow), which is the lever for the triceps. In the dog: Separate from the ulna, which allows limited pronation and supination. Complete and separate. Carries the anconeal process (ununited anconeal process is a clinical condition).

carpal bones.description: Two rows of short bones between the radius and ulna and the metacarpus, forming the carpus (the 'knee' of large animals). In the dog: 7 bones; the radial and intermediate carpal bones are fused into the intermedioradial carpal bone.

metacarpal bones.description: Bones between the carpus and the digits. Their number depends on how many digits the species has. In the dog: Five metacarpals. Mc I (dewclaw) is small; III and IV are the longest.

phalanges of the forelimb.description: Bones of the digits: proximal, middle and distal phalanges, with associated sesamoid bones. In the dog: Five digits; digit I (dewclaw) has two phalanges, digits II–V have three. The distal phalanx carries the claw.

hip bone.description: Formed by the fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis, which meet at the acetabulum. The two hip bones, the sacrum and the first caudal vertebrae form the pelvis. In the dog: The iliac wing is almost vertical (sagittal).

femur.description: The bone of the thigh, between the hip and the stifle. In the dog: No third trochanter; slender shaft. Sesamoid bones (fabellae) lie behind the condyles.

tibia and fibula.description: The main bone of the leg (crus), between the stifle and the hock. Slender lateral bone of the leg (crus), alongside the tibia. In the dog: The fibula is complete, slender and separate. Complete, slender and separate.

tarsal bones.description: Short bones of the hock, between the tibia and the metatarsus. The calcaneal tuber forms the point of the hock. In the dog: 7 bones.

metatarsal bones.description: Bones between the tarsus and the digits of the hindlimb. In the dog: Usually four (Mt II–V). Mt I is often absent or vestigial (the hind dewclaw varies).

phalanges of the hindlimb.description: Bones of the digits of the hindlimb, arranged like those of the forelimb. In the dog: Usually four digits (II–V); a hind dewclaw is variable.
